title: Christians are not market-place charlatans
source_text: Ἴδωμεν δ᾿ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς οὕτως ἔχοντα· ἀλλ᾿ ὁρῶμεν δή που καὶ τοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς (τὰ) ἐπιῤῥητότατα ἐπιδεικνυμένους καὶ ἀγείροντας εἰς μὲν φρονίμων ἀνδρῶν σύλλογον οὐκ ἄν ποτε παρελθόντας οὐδ᾿ ἐν τούτοις τὰ ἑαυτῶν κατατολμήσαντας ἐπιδεικνύειν. ἔνθα δ᾿ ἂν ὁρῶσι μειράκια καὶ οἰκοτρίβων ὄχλον καὶ ἀνοήτων ἀνθρώπων ὅμιλον. ἐνταῦθα ὠθουμένους τε καὶ καλλωπιζομένους. ὅρα δὲ καὶ ἐν τούτοις, τίνα τρόπον ἡμᾶς συκοφαντεῖ, ἐξομοιῶν τοῖς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς τὰ ἐπιῤῥητότατα ἐπιδεικνυμένοις καὶ ἀγείρουσι. ποῖα δὴ ἐπιῤῥητότατα ἐπιδεικνύμεθα; ἢ τί τούτοις παραπλήσιον πράττομεν, οἱ καὶ δι᾿ ἀναγνωσμάτων καὶ διὰ τῶν εἰς τὰ ἀναγνώσματα διηγήσεων προτρέποντες μὲν ἐπὶ τὴν εἰς τὸν θεὸν τῶν ὅλων εὐσέβειαν καὶ τὰς συνθρόνους ταύτης ἀρετὰς. ἀποτρέποντες δ᾿ ἀπὸ τοῦ καταφρονεῖν τοῦ θείου καὶ πάντων τῶν παρὰ τὸν ὀρθὸν λόγον πραττομένων; καὶ οἱ φιλόσοφοί γ᾿ ἂν εὔξαιντο ἀγείρειν τοσούτους ἀκροατὰς λόγων ἐπὶ τὸ καλὸν παρακαλούντων· ὅπερ πεποιήκασι μάλιστα τῶν Κυνικῶν τινες, δημοσίᾳ πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας διαλεγόμενοι. ἆρ᾿ οὖν καὶ τούτους, μὴ συναθροίζοντας μὲν τοὺς νομιζομένους πεπαιδεῦσθαι καλοῦντας δ᾿ ἀπὸ τῆς τριόδου καὶ συνάγοντας ἀκροατὰς, φήσουσι παραπλησίους εἶναι τοῖς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς τὰ ἐπιῤῥητότατα ἐπιδεικνυμένοις καὶ ἀγείρουσιν; ἀλλ᾿ οὔτε Κέλσος οὔτε τις τῶν ταὐτὰ φρονούντων ἐγκαλοῦσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸ φαινόμενον αὐτοῖς φιλάνθρωπον κινοῦσι λόγους καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἰδιωτικοὺς δήμους.
pass_a_gloss: And let us see also the things following of his, holding thus: but we see surely (δή που) also those in the market-places (ἀγοραῖς) displaying (ἐπιδεικνυμένους) the most disreputable things (ἐπιῤῥητότατα) and collecting (ἀγείροντας, gathering crowds / begging) would never come forward (παρελθόντας) into an assembly (σύλλογον) of sensible men (φρονίμων ἀνδρῶν), nor among these dare (κατατολμήσαντας) to display their own things; but wherever they see youths (μειράκια) and a crowd (ὄχλον) of house-born slaves (οἰκοτρίβων) and a throng (ὅμιλον) of senseless (ἀνοήτων) people, there pushing in (ὠθουμένους) and preening (καλλωπιζομένους). And see also in these things in what way he slanders (συκοφαντεῖ) us, likening (ἐξομοιῶν) [us] to those in the market-places displaying the most disreputable things and collecting. What sort of most disreputable things do we display? Or what similar (παραπλήσιον) to these do we do, we who both through readings (ἀναγνωσμάτων) and through expositions (διηγήσεων) on the readings exhort (προτρέποντες) to piety (εὐσέβειαν) toward the God of the universe (θεὸν τῶν ὅλων) and the virtues co-enthroned (συνθρόνους) with it, and turn away (ἀποτρέποντες) from despising (καταφρονεῖν) the divine (θείου) and all things done contrary to right reason (ὀρθὸν λόγον)? And the philosophers would pray (εὔξαιντο) to collect so many hearers of discourses summoning to the good (καλόν); which especially some of the Cynics (Κυνικῶν) have done, conversing (διαλεγόμενοι) in public (δημοσίᾳ) with those chancing by (παρατυγχάνοντας). Will they then say also these, not gathering those thought to be educated, but calling from the crossroads (τριόδου) and assembling hearers, are like those in the market-places displaying the most disreputable things and collecting? But neither Celsus nor any of those thinking the same things accuses (ἐγκαλοῦσι) those who according to what appears to them humane (φιλάνθρωπον) set discourses in motion (κινοῦσι λόγους) also toward the unlearned common people (ἰδιωτικοὺς δήμους).
pass_b_english: Let us look also at what follows in his text, which runs thus: “But surely we see, too, that those who put on the most disreputable displays in the market-places and go round collecting would never come forward into a gathering of sensible men, nor dare to put on their own show among them; but wherever they see adolescents, a crowd of house-slaves and a throng of foolish people, there they push their way in and preen themselves.”

See how he slanders us here as well, likening us to those who put on the most disreputable displays in the market-places and go round collecting. What are these most disreputable displays of ours? Or what do we do that resembles theirs, we who, through readings and through expositions of the readings, urge people to piety toward the God of the universe and to the virtues that share its throne, and turn them away from contempt for the divine and from everything done against right reason?

Philosophers, indeed, would pray to collect so many hearers for discourses that summon them to what is good; and this is what some of the Cynics in particular have done, conversing in public with whoever happens to be passing. Will they say, then, that these men too, who do not gather those thought to be educated but call hearers from the crossroads and bring them together, are like those who put on the most disreputable displays in the market-places and go round collecting? Yet neither Celsus nor anyone who thinks as he does finds fault with those who, out of what they regard as love for humanity, address their discourses even to the common, uneducated people.

choices.choice: ἀγείροντας (from ἀγείρω) means both 'gathering a crowd' and 'begging, taking up collections' (cf. ἀγύρτης, the begging charlatan); 'go round collecting' keeps both senses, which Origen exploits when he says philosophers would pray to 'collect' so many hearers. ἐπιῤῥητότατα: 'the most disreputable (notorious) things'; the bracketed article (τὰ) is Koetschau's supplement. τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἐπιδεικνύειν is rendered 'put on their own show' and καλλωπιζομένους 'preen themselves', so that the two verbs stay distinct (the same choices are used where Origen repeats the charge in 3.52-53). 'Readings and expositions of the readings' refers to the public reading of Scripture and its exposition in Christian assemblies; no specific passage is quoted. 'Right reason' renders ὀρθὸς λόγος, a Stoic term. No Scripture quotation in this chapter.

Celsus's quotation: added 'too' for καί; τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἐπιδεικνύειν 'show off their wares' -> 'put on their own show' (no added image of wares); καλλωπιζομένους 'show off' -> 'preen themselves', so it no longer repeats the word used for ἐπιδεικνύειν.
Kept the superlative in Origen's retort: 'What are these most disreputable displays of ours?'
Joined the fragment 'We who ...' to the question it belongs to, and removed the doubled 'toward ... toward'.
